name: Netlify
description: Static SPAs and Next.js through Netlify's adapter, with an /api proxy in netlify.toml or _redirects.

specSections.title: Environments & Configuration
specSections.guidance: Per environment (production; preview = the version branch built as a branch deploy): the Netlify site URL, every env var per context (production, deploy-preview, branch-deploy) with build-time public values marked, the origin model (proxy via API_ORIGIN and the generated _redirects, or cross-origin with API_BASE_URL and CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS) and the backend URL each environment targets.

requiredEnv.description: The backend target URL for this environment; the frontend platform proxies /api/* to it (FR-146). Derived by AIDE.

true where the environment has its own database (production; preview when a preview database exists), else false. The build runs the data pack's migrate command only when true (FR-154, D-V4-13). Derived by AIDE.
requiredEnv.when: nextjsMode == full-stack && data != none && data != data-supabase && databaseHost != none

checklist.item: netlify.toml has [build] ignore that exits 0 for aide/* branches
Proxy origin model: _redirects is generated at build from API_ORIGIN; no backend host is hard-coded in netlify.toml or a committed _redirects
The SPA fallback is the last rule and no committed _redirects has a catch-all that shadows /api/*
netlify.toml command and publish directory match the frontend pack's build output
Next.js full-stack migrations run only in the build gated by AIDE_RUN_MIGRATIONS
No tokens, site ids or .netlify/ in the repo
No CI job, script or package script deploys with the Netlify CLI; AIDE triggers every deploy
.env.example lists every variable the app needs, with placeholders only
